about.title: About SC Companion
about.subtitle: Who runs this site, what it does, and where the code lives.

what.title: What is this?
what.p1: Star Citizen Companion (SCC) is a free, non-commercial companion app for the space sim Star Citizen: Verse news, a ship and equipment codex, and personal hangar and loadout tools.
what.p2: News, codex and release notes are browsable without an account. An account is only needed for personal features such as your hangar, and registration is currently invite-only.

openSource.title: Open source
openSource.p1: The entire application is developed in the open. Every change is publicly reviewable on GitHub — this is the same code that runs on this site.

data.title: Your data
data.p1: SCC shows no ads and stores only what the features need. Product analytics run through PostHog on EU servers. Details are in the privacy policy:

affiliation.title: Fan project — not affiliated
affiliation.p1: SCC is an unofficial fan project made by the community. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Cloud Imperium Games or Roberts Space Industries, and it never asks for your RSI account credentials.

contact.title: Contact
contact.p1: The fastest way to reach the maintainers:

summary.title: In short
summary.noTracking: No advertising trackers. Product analytics run through PostHog on EU servers to improve the app.
summary.minimal: Only the data the features need — nothing is sold or shared for marketing.
summary.euHosting: Application data is stored in the EU (Supabase, region eu-central-1 / Frankfurt).

hosting.title: Hosting and server logs
hosting.p1: This site is delivered by Vercel Inc. (USA). When you visit, Vercel technically processes your IP address and browser information to serve the page and to protect the service (legitimate interest, Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR).
hosting.p2: The app itself is a static web application; there is no server-side page rendering with personal data.

account.title: Account and application data
account.p1: If you create an account, your e-mail address and a salted password hash are processed by our backend provider Supabase in the EU region eu-central-1 (Frankfurt). Optionally you can sign in with Google; in that case Google learns that you signed in to this site, and we receive your e-mail address from Google.
account.p2: Feature data you create (profile, hangar ships, loadouts, settings) is stored under your account and is only readable by you — enforced with row-level security in the database.
account.p3: Accounts are invite-only. Sign-ups that are not approved can be removed together with their data.

local.title: Cookies and local storage
local.p1: SCC sets no third-party tracking cookies. Your browser's local storage keeps the sign-in session token, language preference and UI state. As an installable web app (PWA), a service worker caches static assets on your device for faster loading and offline use — this cache contains no personal data and can be cleared by uninstalling the app or clearing site data.

thirdParty.title: Third-party services
thirdParty.p1: The app talks to a small, fixed set of services (also technically enforced by our Content-Security-Policy):
thirdParty.vercel: Vercel (hosting, CDN) — delivery of the static app.
thirdParty.google: Google Sign-In (optional) — only if you choose to sign in with Google.
thirdParty.posthog: PostHog (product analytics and error diagnostics) — EU cloud, loaded through a first-party proxy; captures usage events and errors to improve the app.
thirdParty.fonts: Google Fonts — font files are loaded from Google servers; Google may see your IP address.
thirdParty.gameApis: Public Star Citizen data: status.robertsspaceindustries.com and api.star-citizen.wiki (read-only, no account data is sent).

rights.title: Your rights
rights.p1: Under the GDPR you have the right to access, rectification, erasure, restriction of processing, data portability and objection regarding your personal data.
rights.p2: You can delete your account and its data in the app settings, or contact the maintainers via the site notice — we will handle requests promptly.

operator.title: Operator
operator.p1: Star Citizen Companion (sc-companion.vercel.app) is a non-commercial, open-source community project. It is maintained by the StarOrga organization and its contributors on GitHub.
operator.p2: The project earns no revenue: no ads, no paid features, no sponsoring.

liability.title: Liability for content and links
liability.p1: The contents of this site are created with care; nevertheless no guarantee is taken for correctness, completeness or timeliness. Game data shown in the codex is community-extracted and may deviate from the live game.
liability.p2: External links lead to third-party content over which we have no control; at the time of linking no legal violations were apparent. If we become aware of violations, affected links will be removed.

printGuide.title: 3D Printing Guide
printGuide.subtitle: How the community turns Star Citizen ships into printable models — using your own game files, on your own machine.

legal.title: Viewing is fine — downloads are not
legal.p1: You can inspect ship models right here in the codex (3D viewer): rendering game content for VIEWING is the established community practice that CIG tolerates across fan tools — the same ground every ship viewer site stands on. It remains a tolerated grey area, not a granted right.
legal.p2: What this app deliberately does NOT offer: extracted geometry for download or redistribution. The RSI EULA prohibits redistributing extracted game assets, the Fankit & Fandom FAQ rules out offering game content for download by others, and downloadable models collide with CIG’s own licensed model program. So this page explains the workflow you run yourself, on your own machine, with your own game files.
legal.affiliation: This is an unofficial fan site, not affiliated with the Cloud Imperium group of companies. Star Citizen® is a registered trademark of Cloud Imperium Rights LLC.

extract.title: 1. Extract from your own Data.p4k
extract.text: Use a local extraction tool (unp4k, StarFab) against the Data.p4k of your own Star Citizen installation to pull the CryEngine geometry files (.cgf / .cga) of the ship you want.

convert.title: 2. Convert to a standard mesh format
convert.text: Convert the CryEngine chunk files to COLLADA/glTF with Cryengine-Converter or StarBreaker, or import them into Blender directly via SCExporter.

prep.title: 3. Prepare for printing in Blender
prep.text: Game meshes are not watertight. Apply a Solidify modifier for wall thickness, then a Remesh pass to close holes and reduce sub-millimetre detail before exporting STL/3MF.

slice.title: 4. Slice and print
slice.text: Import the STL into your slicer, scale it (game units are not millimetres — use the real ship dimensions from our Codex as reference), add supports and print.

tools.title: Vetted community tools
tools.hint: All tools are third-party, open-source projects you run locally. Check each project's documentation and license before use.
tools.unp4k: The classic Data.p4k extractor — unpacks game archive entries onto your disk.
tools.starfab: Extraction front-end and data tooling for Star Citizen (StarFab GUI on top of scdatatools).
tools.starbreaker: Rust toolkit that reads game data and exports meshes to glTF/GLB.
tools.cryengineConverter: Converts CryEngine .cgf/.cga chunk files into COLLADA for Blender import.
tools.scexporter: Blender add-on that imports Star Citizen geometry directly.

tips.title: Print-prep tips
tips.watertight: Game meshes are display meshes: expect holes, intersecting shells and non-manifold edges — they always need repair before slicing.
tips.solidify: Blender's Solidify modifier gives paper-thin hull panels a printable wall thickness (0.8–1.6 mm at desk-model scale).
tips.remesh: A voxel Remesh pass closes gaps and merges shells at the cost of fine detail — pick the voxel size to match your printer's resolution.
tips.scale: There is no canonical scale in the files. Scale by real dimensions: look up the ship's length in the Codex and scale the model to your target size.
tips.lod: Prefer the highest LOD (LOD0) for hero prints; lower LODs slice faster and are fine for small desk models.
tips.cigGuide: CIG community guide: Easy preparation of STL files for 3D printing

privacy.gameContentOnly: The extension reads personalised game content only — the ship names on your own RSI hangar page. No personal data is collected.
privacy.noCredentials: No credentials, cookies or session tokens are read.
privacy.noPersonalData: No account name, e-mail address, pledge value or order data is read.

privacy.localOnly: Only a checksum of your fleet and the time of the last import are stored, locally in your browser.

install.title: Hangar import — browser extension
install.subtitle: Star Citizen Companion cannot read robertsspaceindustries.com by itself: browsers forbid one site from reading another. A small browser extension can read the hangar page you are already looking at — and hand the ship list to your hangar here.

what.title: What it does
what.text: Three steps, and you confirm the last one.

open.title: You open your own hangar at RSI
open.text: Signed in, on your pledges page. The extension does nothing anywhere else.

offer.title: It offers an import — only when there is something new
offer.text: Your fleet is reduced to a checksum. Unchanged hangar, no message. Bought or gifted a ship? The offer comes back on its own.

confirm.title: You confirm here
confirm.text: The ship list opens in Star Citizen Companion with every entry visible. Only the rows you tick are written to your hangar.

privacy.title: What is read — and what is not
privacy.openSource: The extension is part of this project's open repository: every line it runs can be read before you install it.
